page: Amazon Web Services m6g.2xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture running at 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position the m6g.2xlarge in the average tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 12135.21 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5402.0, both falling within the middle 50% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 472.85 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 120.79 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 945.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.4. Cryptographic and compression tasks also represent a performance tradeoff, with a poor Passmark CPU encryption score of 1083.15 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression speed of 20.34 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the custom ARM-based architecture offers a resource-dense profile that delivers balanced compute and memory capacity without the overhead of x86 licensing or hyperthreading complexities. This makes the instance highly suitable for workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 9.38 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a Passmark database score of 5174.5 and Redis SET performance of 9.56 million operations per second. It is also well-suited for software compilation, containerized microservices, and general-purpose application hosting.
